visibleAssistantStatements.text: The implementation will preserve the existing parser exports and upload shape. The ledger will store only SHA-256 event keys plus token/date tuples, remain bounded to the existing OpenCode limits, keep the first tuple on conflicts, and mark collection partial via a warning. For account switches, it will be keyed by stable `clientSourceId` in connector state, while old source-ID keyed state remains compatible and is migrated only after a complete bounded rescan.

The focused regressions now cover all five JSONL event adapters through real collection state transitions, OpenCode SQLite history deletion, and conflicting tuples. Existing preservation checks expose only assertions intentionally superseded by the new requirement, and the broader config suite passes, including OpenCode’s existing exact-ID cutover acceptance gate; I’m documenting the persistence behavior and then will run the new and requested checks separately.

The self-review identified one privacy gap in the pre-existing Claude incremental state: its per-file/message maps still persisted raw provider message IDs even though the new ledger was hashed. I’m correcting that persisted state to use the same SHA-256 identity representation, updating the security regression to assert hashed keys, then I’ll rerun the focused and preservation checks because this is a final behavioral edit.

The privacy follow-up passes its focused regression, and the three requested suites pass again after the final edit. I’m doing one final full connector test sweep as an additional preservation check, then I’ll inspect status/diff once more and close the task without committing.
